reviews.title: GAME CHANGER! GET IT!
reviews.comment:
My Experience with Fixing Popping Sounds and Poor Audio Playback
Hey everyone, here’s the deal:
I’ve been battling nonstop audio issues on my system since I built it. My setup includes:
Motherboard: ASUS ROG STRIX Z790-E Gaming WiFi
Audio: Onboard Realtek sound
Speakers: Dell Altec Lansing ADA995 THX 5.1
The Problem:
From day one, I’ve had relentless popping sounds. It wasn’t terrible for music or movies, but every new audio event caused a pop at the start. To make matters worse, only the left and right speakers worked properly. During a Windows speaker test, I could hear sound from all speakers (center, left, right, and rear), but in actual playback, I couldn’t get all speakers to work together, no matter what I did.
I’ve spent 20+ years in IT, so I tried everything:
Disabled power-saving modes for the Realtek card using a registry hack (worked temporarily on another system).
Tried installing the latest drivers through ASUS Armory Crate.
Disabled the virtual driver, installed Realtek's app from the Microsoft Store, and downloaded every piece of software from ASUS and Realtek.
Reinstalled drivers at least 10 times (as of January 2025).
Nothing worked. The sound quality remained poor, the popping persisted, and my speakers refused to cooperate in harmony.
The Solution:
This week, I hit my breaking point and decided to try a dedicated sound card. I ordered the Creative Sound BlasterX AE-5 Plus SABRE32-class Hi-res Gaming Sound Card off Amazon for around $130.
Holy. Crap. What a difference.
All my speakers now work beautifully.
The card includes an amazing built-in EQ, which lets me adjust individual speaker volumes. I cranked up the rears, boosted bass, treble, and mids, and tweaked everything to perfection.
No more popping sounds. My system now sounds 3X better.
I also downloaded Sound Blaster Command (Creative’s software), which is surprisingly excellent. I typically avoid letting extra software run on my system, but this one stays. It’s my digital EQ and totally worth it.
Pros:
Crystal-clear audio, no more popping.
Full control over individual speaker volumes and EQ settings.
My 5.1 system finally delivers the sound quality I’ve been chasing for years.
Music sounds incredible, and my system cranks like never before.
Cons:
There’s a bit of reverb from Sound Blaster Command that I’d love to reduce by about 25%, but I haven’t found the setting yet.
Final Thoughts:
If you’ve been suffering through Realtek’s onboard audio issues like I have, do yourself a favor and invest in this sound card. This upgrade has been a total game-changer for me.
Thanks, Sound Blaster, for bringing joy back to my audio setup. Realtek, on the other hand... well, you know where I stand.
I hope this helps someone out there!
Cheers,
A happy human (soon to be deaf).

reviews.title: Rich full sound, quirky software.
reviews.comment:
The software on this, is a little strange but nothing an afternoon playing around with the varying settings can't fix. That said, this is an incredibly solid little unit. My other sound card was an Asus Essence STX. Putting this card in, solved a lot of strange quirks the other card had, straight away that I thought was a receiver problem, as I run the pc to my Yamaha receiver. I could never get the surround sound to work right with the receiver, nor get the Dolby or DTS to truly work. Somehow the encoder on it, wasn't compatible with the receiver. That said, I had zero issues with that on the Creative here. It immediately received the signal, went right into surround and I've been off to the races since.
There's a lot more sound settings you can adjust on this card than the asus unit I had, and it's incredible how much difference every sound setting can make. I started with the equalizer, much like I did with the asus. But unlike the asus, I could tell it exactly what kind of speakers I have, in addition to their placement.
The sound itself, is dramatically fuller and warm. The RGB is a nice touch and addition to the pc of course, and the leds themselves seem to be of a pretty good color range compared to some other products out there. There is also decidedly less coil whine coming from my pc now, and a lot of strange foibles I had with sound sources, are gone.
Having had the Essence for seven or eight years, and coming to this one I've got a pretty good comparison. Both are great, this one's better. Both blow away the motherboard mounted stuff, by a long ways. Of the two, I'd recommend this, every time. It sounds better than the Essence II, as well (which a friend has).
